newsitem.title: USA: Trump Hotels in joint venture with Colony Capital.
newsitem.headline: Trump Hotels in joint venture with Colony Capital.

text.p: Trump Hotels & Casino Resorts, Inc. and Trump Hotels & Casino Resorts Holdings, L.P., controlled by mogul Donald Trump, said Monday they plan to expand and renovate Trump's Castle in Atlantic City, N.J., financed through the sale of a 51 percent interest in the property.
Under a funding and joint venture agreement, Los Angeles-based real estate investment firm Colony Capital Inc. will purchase 51 percent of Trump's Castle for $125 million.
The current Trump's Castle debt of $314 million will be split off from Trump Hotels & Casino Resorts' balance sheet upon completion of the transaction, the Trump organisations said.
Trump Hotels & Casino Resorts Holdings will retain a 49 percent stake in Trump's Castle and will continue to manage the property.

The hotel will be renamed the Trump Marina, and according to Donald Trump, will be the only casino located on the marina waterfront. It will be "highlighted by its 645 slip marina, the East Coast's largest," he said in a statement.

Proceeds from the transaction will provide the necessary resources for the renovation of the new Trump Marina, said Nicholas Ribis, president and chief executive officer of Trump Hotels. The number of rooms will increase to 1,500 from 728.

Donald Trump, the New York real estate tycoon who as a rule names all of his property after himself, owns several pieces of prime real estate in Manhattan, including Trump Tower on Fifth Avenue. His companies also own Trump Plaza Hotel & Casino and Trump Taj Mahal Casino Resort in Atlantic City, N.J., as well as Trump Indiana, the riverboat casino at Buffington Harbour, Ind. on Lake Michigan
Trump Hotels stock was up $1.50 at $11.625 in morning trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
